and a red build comes back to the next round as its brief. Say in your
final message that the round ran no tests here.

YOUR ROUND is the `tdd-loop` skill's three phases, in order, no steps
skipped: one failing test for the smallest facet that moves an acceptance
test closer to green, then the least code that passes it, then refactor
with the bar green. Never edit an acceptance test to make it pass — if an
acceptance test is wrong, stop and say so; that is a failed round.

Under `parallel-change`, all of this happens in the NEW module: leave the
old code alone and working until the acceptance tests are green, and make
the caller switch its own round. Under `characterize`, the
characterization tests are part of the green bar you must keep — a
refactor that reddens them is a behaviour change. Under `mechanical`,
there is no red phase at all: perform the exact edits its Facets
record and commit; the EXISTING tests `.lore/dod.md` names are CI's to
run, and its verdict says whether they stayed green. The diff is the
deliverable, and a round that invents a new test for it has left the
strategy.

readFileSync of a src/ or test file, a regex over another test,

  for anything this ticket did not write, and never by discarding your own
  work. This is why a nine-day-old branch stalled: 186 commits of drift,
  no checks, and a wait with nothing to wait for.

THE LAST LINE YOU PRINT is how the round ends. Print exactly one, on its

the ticket is done — the build decides that, after your push. You are

  LORE_NODE_RESULT: {"outcome":"success","extras":{"tdd_done":"<the facet you closed>","tdd_next":"<the facet the next round takes, or 'acceptance green'>"}}

  in `.lore/dod.md` is closed, its acceptance tests pass, AND no

  LORE_NODE_RESULT: {"outcome":"success","extras":{"tdd_next":"acceptance green"}}

## Why

OLT's TMS API description is public and needs no key: `https://olt.dora-apps.com/api/ext/v1/openapi.json`, with the guide as Markdown at `/guide.md`. On 11 November we compared it with Otto's copy, `api/tms-openapi.json`, committed 15 October. DOA has only added things since: invoices, invoice lines, carriers, fixed routes, recurring orders and a few fields. Nothing Otto calls was removed.

Three of the changes make `get_booking_status` give a customer a wrong answer once Otto reads the real TMS (#401):

1. **Current order numbers are refused.** The guide now gives order numbers as `PPP-ÅÅÅÅ-NNNNNN`, for example `OLT-2026-000123`. The haulier sets the prefix, and older numbers can have fewer digits, so the guide says to read the number as text. Otto accepts only `^OLT-\d{4}-\d{4}$` (`apps/api/src/tools/bookingStatus/mapping.ts:7`), and `bookingFor` answers any other input with the not-found card without asking the TMS (`tool.ts:64-76`, FR-115). A customer asking about a current order is told it doesn't exist. The tool's description and example prompts also teach the model the four-digit shape (`tool.ts:23-29`).
2. **A split shipment shows as cancelled.** A dispatcher can split a shipment into legs at a terminal. The original then keeps the status `ANNULLERET`, with `splittet: true` and `splittetI`, the number of active legs. The legs are listed in `legs` and carry `parentShipmentReference`. ## Why

OLT's production runs Otto's MongoDB from `modules/otto-mongo` in re-cinq/infrastructure. `projects/olt/otto.tf` calls it with its defaults: one replica, and a 10Gi volume on the cluster's default storage class. The module's own header says it is for re:cinq's test environment only, that "nothing here backs the volume up or survives losing it", and that real customer conversations need a managed database. Nothing in re-cinq/infrastructure configures a backup for it. We could not check the live project for snapshots set up outside Terraform, because the Otto team has no access to `recinq-olt-production` (KU-30).

If that volume is lost, so is everything Otto keeps, with no second copy:

- `hal_sessions`: customers' conversations, kept 30 days;
- `escalations`: hand-offs, including ones not yet delivered;
- `auditEntries`: the audit trail, kept 365 days as compliance evidence (#306);
- `conversationAccessLog`: who read which customer's conversation;
- `erasureReceipts`: the proof that erasure requests were carried out;
- `feedbackRatings` and `loginSessions`.

The audit trail, the access log and the erasure receipts are records OLT may have to show an auditor.

One replica also means any move of the pod is downtime. On Autopilot a node upgrade can leave a zonal disk attached to the old node for a long time; lore#4095 measured 40 minutes for Lore's Dgraph.

## What to do

Decide between two routes, then build the chosen one in re-cinq/infrastructure:

1. **A managed database** in the EU, such as MongoDB Atlas in `europe-west1`. It adds a sub-processor, which the processing agreement with OLT must cover.
2. **Keep the in-cluster MongoDB and back it up:** a scheduled snapshot of its disk (a Compute Engine snapshot schedule, or Backup for GKE) or a scheduled `mongodump` to a bucket in `europe-west1`, with a retention period and a restore that has been tried once.

Either way:

- Backups hold conversations past the 30-day sweep and past erasure requests. Their retention must be short, approved and written down, and `docs/runbooks/gdpr-erasure.md` must say what a restore brings back and how erasures are applied again after one.
- ADR-003's storage row should name where the data and its backups live.

The module header also notes that the generated root password lives in the Terraform state bucket; worth deciding at the same time whether that stays.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Production's MongoDB data survives losing its volume: a backup, or a managed database's own replication and backups, exists in the EU and is declared in Terraform.
- [ ] A restore into a scratch namespace or database has been done once, recording how long it took and how old the restored data was.
- [ ] The backups' retention period is stated, with who approved it.
- [ ] `docs/runbooks/gdpr-erasure.md` says what a restore brings back and how erasures are applied again after one.
- [ ] ADR-003 records the database and its backups.
